title: Hero secondary (WhatsApp) CTA renders white-on-white — label and icon are invisible
evidence: crop-hero.png + desktop-home-true.png show an empty white rounded pill to the right of the green CTA where the WhatsApp button should be. Code: primitives.tsx BG_VAR has no `white` key (lines 149-156); ink surface forces white text (line 155); hero_image.tsx renders `<ChunkyButton bg="white">` (line 182) inside the ink BentoCard (line 89). Orchestrator measured bg rgb(255,255,255) AND color rgb(255,255,255).
rootCause: ChunkyButton bg="white" maps to BG_MAP.white="bg-white" but there is NO BG_VAR["white"] entry (primitives.tsx lines 133-156), so surfaceStyle("white") returns no `color`. The hero wraps the CTA group inside a BentoCard bg="ink" (hero_image.tsx line 89, when hasImage), and ink's surfaceStyle sets `color:"#fff"` (primitives.tsx line 155). That white text color cascades into the white-background button → white text + white WhatsApp glyph on white fill = 1:1 contrast, fully invisible. It reads as an empty white pill in crop-hero.png / desktop-home-true.png.
fix: Make the white/cream surfaces self-contained: add `white: { bg: "#ffffff", fg: "var(--bk-ink,#1a1a1a)" }` (and a matching cream entry) to BG_VAR in primitives.tsx so every surface explicitly sets its own ink foreground and never inherits a parent's white text. Belt-and-suspenders: in buttonStyle()/surfaceStyle(), default `color` to `var(--bk-ink,#1a1a1a)` whenever the surface is light. This fixes the hero WhatsApp button and any future `bg="white"` ChunkyButton/Sticker placed on a dark surface.
note: Confirmed and accurately located. BG_VAR (primitives.tsx:149-156) has no `white` key, so surfaceStyle("white") sets no `color`; the white ChunkyButton (hero_image.tsx:182) sits inside BentoCard bg="ink" (hero_image.tsx:89, when hasImage) whose surfaceStyle forces color:#fff (line 155), cascading into the white-bg button. WhatsAppIcon uses fill="currentColor" (primitives.tsx:382), so icon is white too → white label + white glyph on white pill. crop-hero.png shows the empty white pill right of the green CTA with only a faint drop-shadow outline (the 1px #1a1a1a drop-shadow on the icon). Root cause, evidence, and proposed fix all hold. P0 justified: secondary WhatsApp CTA is invisible on every image-backed hero (the default), breaking a primary COD conversion path.

title: content-visibility intrinsic-size over-reserves height → thousands of px of phantom blank space and inflated scrollbar
location: packages/sections/src/_lazy-section.tsx:28,36-37; packages/sections/src/RenderSection.tsx:178-186 (esp. line 182, no intrinsicSize passed); evidence tmp/audit/desktop-home-true.png
evidence: desktop-home-true.png (1080-tall viewport capture) shows content ending ~y=340 with the rest of the frame blank, confirming inflated layout height below the fold. Code: _lazy-section.tsx `intrinsicSize = "auto 1200px"` (line 28) applied uniformly; RenderSection.tsx wraps all idx>=2 sections in LazySection (lines 178-186).
rootCause: Every below-fold section is wrapped by LazySection with a hardcoded `containIntrinsicSize: "auto 1200px"` default (_lazy-section.tsx lines 28-30) and the page has many sections (RenderSection imports ~50 types; EAGER_SECTION_COUNT=2 so everything after the first 2 is lazy). Until each section scrolls near the viewport the browser reserves a flat 1200px placeholder per section regardless of its real (often much shorter, e.g. marquee/trust strip ~60-120px) height. Summed across all deferred sections this inflates total document height far beyond real content (orchestrator: ~7543px scroll vs ~4379px real desktop → ~3160px phantom void) and produces a wrong, oversized scrollbar.
fix: Use the `auto` keyword alone (`containIntrinsicSize: "auto auto"` / `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 0`) so the browser remembers each element's last-rendered size instead of forcing a flat 1200px, OR pass a realistic per-section-type estimate from the registry (strips ~120px, hero ~440px, grids taller). Eliminates the phantom void and fixes the scrollbar.
note: Code & screenshot confirm: every below-fold section (idx>=EAGER_SECTION_COUNT=2) is wrapped by LazySection with NO intrinsicSize prop, so the default "auto 1200px" applies uniformly (RenderSection.tsx:182 passes only key+sectionId; _lazy-section.tsx:28 default). desktop-home-true.png shows the large blank void below the category grid. BUT the finding misreads CSS semantics and is over-severe: "auto 1200px" is the auto-keyword form — the browser latches each element's REAL last-rendered size once it has rendered, so 1200px is only the fallback for never-yet-seen sections, not a permanent flat reservation. The over-reservation is transient (self-corrects as the user scrolls past each section), so the "3160px permanent phantom void / wrong scrollbar" framing overstates it. The proposed fix is partly wrong: the code already uses `auto`; switching the fallback to `0`/`auto auto` would HURT scroll-anchor stability for unseen sections — only the registry-per-type-estimate suggestion is sound. Real polish/perf defect, correctly located, but P2 not P1.

title: Up to THREE concurrent font sources: next/font (self-hosted) + two more runtime Google Fonts <link>s built per-tenant (legacy design_tokens AND brand-kit), risk of duplicate render-blocking font fetches
evidence: Three independent font pipelines coexist: (1) next/font self-hosts Bricolage_Grotesque + DM_Sans (layout.tsx:5-17); (2) tenant layout builds `googleFontsUrl` from legacy `dt.fonts` and injects `<link rel=stylesheet href={googleFontsUrl}>` (s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:84-90, 206-209); (3) it ALSO builds `bkFontsUrl` via buildBrandKitFontsUrl and injects a SECOND `<link>` (s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:170, 210-213). buildBrandKitFontsUrl (packages/shared/src/brand-kit-vars.ts:368-387) only skips 'Bricolage Grotesque'/'DM Sans' for the brand-kit path, but the LEGACY `googleFontsUrl` path at layout.tsx:88-90 has NO skip set — so a tenant whose design_tokens.fonts.body='DM Sans' re-downloads DM Sans from the CDN even though next/font already self-hosts it (this is exactly the orchestrator's 'DM Sans loads from BOTH next/font AND Google Fonts CDN' observation). Both runtime links are render-blocking stylesheets to fonts.googleapis.com with no preconnect.
rootCause: Two font systems (legacy design_tokens + new brand_kit) were never reconciled after the brand-kit migration; the legacy path lacks the de-dupe skip set the new path has.
fix: Collapse to ONE font path. Delete the legacy `googleFontsUrl` block (layout.tsx:84-90, 206-209) — the brand-kit path supersedes it. Pass the same skip set used by buildBrandKitFontsUrl to any remaining builder so self-hosted fonts (Bricolage/DM Sans) are never re-fetched from the CDN. For the brand-kit <link>, add `<link rel=preconnect href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>` and prefer next/font/google with a dynamic subset, or accept the link but never duplicate a self-hosted family. Net: at most one external font request, only when a tenant picks a non-bundled family.
note: Real and accurate: tenant layout emits both a legacy googleFontsUrl <link> (layout.tsx:84-90,206-209) and a brand-kit bkFontsUrl <link> (170,210-213); buildBrandKitFontsUrl skips self-hosted Bricolage/DM Sans (brand-kit-vars.ts:368-387) but the legacy path has NO skip set, so dt.fonts.body='DM Sans' re-fetches an already self-hosted family. Both are render-blocking with no fonts.gstatic.com preconnect (grep: none). One mis-cite: next/font lives in ROOT apps/storefront/app/layout.tsx:2-17, not the tenant layout '5-17'. Adjusted to P2: real render-blocking/CWV regression but only triggers when a tenant sets custom design_tokens.fonts (vestigial legacy path), so the duplicate is conditional, not universal.

title: content-visibility wrapper hard-codes contain-intrinsic-size to 1200px for EVERY below-fold section — `intrinsicSize` prop is dead, producing a multi-thousand-px phantom blank void + inflated scrollbar
location: packages/sections/src/_lazy-section.tsx:26-43 (default + style) and packages/sections/src/RenderSection.tsx:178-186 (sole call site, no intrinsicSize); grep across packages+apps confirms no other caller; tmp/audit/live-supplementary-findings.md does not contain the cited measurements
evidence: RenderSection.tsx:178-186 wraps each section after the first EAGER_SECTION_COUNT (=2) in `<LazySection sectionId={s.id}>` but NEVER passes `intrinsicSize`. LazySection (_lazy-section.tsx:26-43) therefore always uses the default `intrinsicSize='auto 1200px'`, applied as `style={{ contentVisibility:'auto', containIntrinsicSize:'auto 1200px' }}`. With ~5+ below-fold sections each reserving 1200px while paint-skipped, the reserved height massively exceeds the real ~content height — matching the orchestrator's measurement (reserved ~4379px but scrollHeight inflated to ~7543px desktop → ~3160px phantom void below the fold + a too-long scrollbar). The `intrinsicSize` prop exists in the type but is never wired, so it's dead code masking the bug. NOTE: `containIntrinsicSize:'auto 1200px'` uses the `auto` keyword which should remember the last-rendered size once a section has painted, but on first paint / for never-yet-seen sections the 1200px fallback dominates and creates the void.
rootCause: The lazy-paint optimization shipped with a one-size placeholder and the parameter to fix it (intrinsicSize) was never plumbed through from RenderSection.
fix: Pass a realistic per-section-type intrinsic height instead of a blanket 1200px. Cheapest correct fix: derive a rough height map keyed by section type (e.g. marquee_strip ~80px, trust_strip ~120px, testimonials ~400px, product_grid ~900px) and pass `intrinsicSize={`auto ${estPx}px`}` from RenderSection. Better: drop the explicit px and rely on `content-visibility:auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto none` (let the browser learn the real size after first paint) OR raise EAGER_SECTION_COUNT so the first screenful never gets a wrong reservation. Removing the dead `intrinsicSize` prop or actually using it is required either way.
note: Code defect is REAL and exactly located. _lazy-section.tsx:28 defaults intrinsicSize="auto 1200px" (applied as containIntrinsicSize at :37); RenderSection.tsx:182 is the SOLE LazySection call site and passes only key+sectionId — grep confirms zero other callers and zero other intrinsicSize usages, so the prop is genuinely dead and every below-fold section gets the blanket auto 1200px placeholder. Path is live (v2-page.tsx uses RenderPage). BUT severity is overstated (P1→P2) and the headline evidence is not substantiated: (1) the value is "auto 1200px" not bare "1200px" — the `auto` keyword makes content-visibility:auto remember real size after first paint, so any phantom void exists only for not-yet-scrolled sections and self-corrects on scroll (the finding's own NOTE concedes this); (2) the cited orchestrator measurements (reserved ~4379px, scrollHeight ~7543px, ~3160px void) appear in NO repo artifact — tmp/audit/live-supplementary-findings.md does not contain this finding or those numbers, and they can't be derived from the PNGs. It's a worth-fixing dead-prop/over-tall-placeholder polish issue (slightly too-long initial scrollbar), not a P1 major.

title: PDP image is full-width single-column (next/image `sizes` claims 50vw on desktop but slot is ~100vw → under-fetched & blurry), and zoom modal hard-codes 1600x1600
location: packages/sections/src/pdp_gallery.tsx:138 (stacked sizes) and :186-193 (zoom); packages/sections/src/RenderSection.tsx:158-189 (flat stream, no 2-col); apps/storefront/app/s/[tenant]/products/[slug]/page.tsx:82-89; apps/storefront/app/s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:232-237; screenshot tmp/audit/desktop-pdp.png

The zoom modal (line 186-193) hard-codes `width={1600} height={1600}` regardless of the source's true aspect (e.g. 720x1080) → letterbox/distortion. THEN `sizes="(max-width:768px) 100vw, 50vw"` becomes correct. Until 2-col lands, set the stacked `sizes` to the real slot (`(max-width:1024px) 100vw, 600px` matching the max content width) so the right candidate is fetched. For zoom, drop the fixed 1600x1600 and use the source's intrinsic dimensions (or `fill` in a max-w/max-h container with object-contain) to avoid distortion.
note: Confirmed. pdp_gallery.tsx:138 sets sizes="...,50vw" on the priority LCP main image, but RenderPage (RenderSection.tsx:158-189) renders sections as a flat full-width vertical stream with NO 2-col gallery/buy-box shell, and neither the V2 product page (page.tsx:82-89) nor the tenant layout (layout.tsx:232-237) applies any max-width container — so the slot is ~100vw on desktop and the browser under-fetches/upscales (blurry). tmp/audit/desktop-pdp.png visually confirms full-width single-column gallery with buy-box stacked below. One detail correction: the zoom "distortion/letterbox" sub-claim is overstated — line 192's `w-auto h-auto object-contain` makes the browser honor intrinsic aspect, so 1600x1600 yields no visible distortion (it's only a wrong nominal optimizer/CLS hint, not visual distortion). The sizes under-fetch is the valid load-bearing P1.

title: Analytics pixel injector fires for ANY non-empty pixel id with no format validation — a placeholder/invalid TikTok id (e.g. CABCDEF) still loads analytics.tiktok.com and POSTs live
evidence: analytics-pixels.tsx:46 reads `analytics.tiktok_pixel_id?.trim()` and line 71 gates only on truthiness `{tiktok && (...ttq.load('${escapeJs(tiktok)}'); ttq.page();...)}`. There is no validation that the id is a real pixel id (TikTok ids are ~20-char uppercase alphanumeric, e.g. C…). So if a tenant's config carries a placeholder like 'CABCDEF', the script injects, hits `https://analytics.tiktok.com/i18n/pixel/events.js?sdkid=CABCDEF` and fires `ttq.page()` POSTs (the live console 'Invalid pixel ID' warning the orchestrator saw). Same gap applies to meta/ga/snap ids (all line 45-48 trim-then-truthy). This is wasted 3rd-party JS + network on every page for an analytics call that goes nowhere, and a data-privacy footgun.
rootCause: Pixel injection trusts the raw config string; no schema/format guard between merchant input and live script injection.
fix: Add a per-provider id-shape validator before rendering each <Script>: e.g. tiktok `/^[A-Z0-9]{15,30}$/`, meta `/^\d{15,16}$/`, ga `/^G-[A-Z0-9]{6,}$/`, snap UUID-ish. Skip injection (and log once in dev) when the id fails the regex. This stops placeholder/typo ids from loading 3rd-party pixels and prevents the LCP/INP tax of a doomed analytics request on slow networks. The placeholder value itself is data-config (clear it from the scheniders-iraq tenant), but the missing validation is the code defect that let it ship.
note: Code defect confirmed: analytics-pixels.tsx lines 45-48 trim then gate only on truthiness (lines 52/71/85/105 `{tiktok && ...}`), with zero format validation. AnalyticsConfig (store-config.ts:254) is a bare TS interface — string fields, no Zod/regex guard anywhere in repo (only consumed here + 2 tests). A placeholder like CABCDEF passes and injects the TikTok script + fires ttq.page() to analytics.tiktok.com. Severity adjusted P1→P2: scripts are afterInteractive (non-blocking, not an LCP-blocker), no PII leak — it's a bounded wasted-network/privacy-hygiene defect contingent on bad config; the 'Invalid pixel ID' console warning is cosmetic. Fix is sound but proposed GA regex /^G-[A-Z0-9]{6,}$/ would reject legacy UA- ids.

title: Product-card images use `mix-blend-multiply` — forces an offscreen compositing layer per card, costly on low-end Iraqi devices in a multi-item grid
evidence: product-card.tsx:102-105 applies `className={cn('object-cover mix-blend-multiply', !inStock && 'opacity-60 grayscale')}` to every product image. `mix-blend-multiply` is a non-trivial blend mode that forces the browser to create an isolated compositing layer and re-composite against the tinted parent (TINT_BG, line 15-22) on scroll/paint; multiplied across a grid of cards (product_grid renders up to 8 via defaultProps.query.limit, product_grid.tsx:39-44) this adds GPU/CPU compositing work and can hurt INP/scroll smoothness on budget Android devices common in the Iraq market. It's also a visual hazard (multiply darkens light photos onto the pastel tint).
rootCause: Aesthetic blend applied per-image without weighing the compositing cost across a repeated grid.
fix: Drop `mix-blend-multiply`. If the tinted-photo aesthetic is wanted, achieve it with a cheaper static overlay (a semi-transparent tint div over the image, or a CSS `filter`/background that doesn't require per-element layer isolation), or only apply it on hover. Removing it eliminates per-card compositing layers across the grid.
note: Verified: product-card.tsx:102-105 applies `object-cover mix-blend-multiply` to every grid image; TINT_BG (lines 15-22) sets light pastel `/30` tints behind it; product_grid.tsx defaultProps.query.limit=8 (line 40) and the grid maps each item to SchneidersProductCard (lines 124-136, up to 4 cols). mix-blend-multiply does force blend-mode isolation (separate buffer + re-composite against the tinted backdrop) per image — real per-card paint/compositing cost, and on light product photos it visibly darkens them onto the pastel tint (visual hazard is the stronger half of the claim). Minor correction: the grid file is packages/sections/src/product_grid.tsx (not src/sections/), and the limit is line 40, not 39-44. The "re-composites on every scroll frame" framing is slightly overstated (browsers cache the static composite; cost is mainly at paint), so P2 — not higher — is correct; the proposed fix (cheaper static tint overlay or hover-only blend) is sound.

title: RenderSection is a client component that side-effect-imports all 47 sections — every page ships JS for sections it never renders (oversized client hydration bundle)
evidence: RenderSection.tsx:11 declares `"use client"`, then lines 26-72 side-effect import all 47 section modules (`import './hero_image'; ... './checkout_form'; ... './site_footer';`) to populate the client-side registry (the comment at 21-25 explains the empty-registry-on-client problem). Because RenderSection is a client component pulled in by V2Page→RenderPage, the home page's client bundle includes the code for checkout_form, pdp_buy_box, pdp_gallery, order_tracker, cart_summary, etc. — none of which render on the home route. Each section also imports the 'use client' primitives.tsx and next/image. This inflates the JS the browser must download + hydrate on a content page that is mostly static, hurting INP/TBT on mobile.
rootCause: The 'register every section in the client graph' workaround imports the entire section catalog into the client bundle to dodge an empty-registry problem, instead of code-splitting per section type.
fix: Split the registry so server and client graphs share registration without forcing every section into the client bundle. Options: (a) make RenderSection a SERVER component (the page is server-rendered anyway) and only the genuinely-interactive sections (pdp_gallery, testimonials_carousel, checkout_form, newsletter, etc.) carry their own 'use client' — most display sections (hero, trust_strip, marquee, category_grid, brand_story) have no interactivity and don't need client JS; (b) keep RenderSection client but lazy/dynamic-import section renderers by type via next/dynamic so only the sections actually present on a given page are bundled/hydrated. Either way, the home route stops shipping checkout/PDP/cart section code.
note: Verified the full chain. RenderSection.tsx:11 is "use client"; lines 26-72 are 47 bare side-effect imports. Each section self-registers at module top-level (e.g. checkout_form.tsx:363 registerSection(definition)), a real side effect webpack's sideEffects pruning cannot tree-shake. RenderPage exported from that same client module is rendered by V2Page (async server component, v2-page.tsx:110), which the home route renders (app/s/[tenant]/page.tsx:70). So the home page's client bundle includes interactive sections it never renders — checkout_form (its own "use client"+useState), pdp_*, cart_*, order_tracker. Fix premise holds: hero_image.tsx has no "use client" and needn't ship client JS. Real, accurately located, P2 (bundle/INP/TBT regression on mobile, not a correctness/trust break — SSR still renders sections fine).

title: category_grid / brand_story render a flat gradient placeholder div when image_url is unset — looks unfinished and the empty card has no reserved aspect ratio for the eventual image (CLS risk)
evidence: category_grid.tsx:127-143 renders `<Image src={c.image_url} ... priority={i < props.columns} />` only when `c.image_url` exists, else falls through to a `bg-gradient-to-t from-candy-ink/60...` div (line 143) with only a low-contrast corner label — exactly the orchestrator's 'giant flat gradient blocks, no image/icon, tiny labels'. brand_story.tsx:113-123 does the same: `<Image src={props.accent_image_url} />` when set, else `<div className='absolute inset-0 bg-gradient-to-br from-candy-lilac...'>` (the empty 558x288 lilac placeholder the orchestrator saw). Reserve a fixed aspect-ratio box (e.g. `aspect-[4/3]`) for both the image and the placeholder so swapping in a real image causes zero CLS. Primary fix is data (upload category + brand-story imagery for scheniders-iraq), but ship a presentable fallback so an unconfigured store still looks intentional.
note: Fallback-quality half is real and accurately located: category_grid.tsx:127-143 renders a bare gradient+corner-label when c.image_url is unset; brand_story.tsx:113-123 renders a bare bg-gradient-to-br lilac div when accent_image_url is unset. No icon/initial empty state. But the CLS half is wrong: the box is already reserved — category_grid's BentoCard has aspect-square (line 124) and brand_story's has min-h-[280px] (line 111), and both branches share that same parent with the image using fill/absolute, so swapping in a real image causes zero layout shift. Since the CLS rationale (which placed it in the Performance/CWV dimension at P2) is false, this is a cosmetic empty-state polish nit, data-config driven (tenant has no imagery) → P3, not a performance finding.

title: No `quality` tuning and no blur/LQIP placeholders on any next/image — default q=75 full transcodes + blank-then-pop image loads add avoidable bytes and CLS/flash on slow networks
location: hero_image.tsx:102-110, helpers/product-card.tsx:96-106, pdp_gallery.tsx:134-141, category_grid.tsx:128-139, brand_story.tsx:114-121; apps/storefront/next.config.ts:6-22
evidence: Across hero_image.tsx, product-card.tsx (line 96-106), pdp_gallery.tsx (134-141), category_grid.tsx (128), brand_story.tsx (114) NO <Image> sets `quality` or `placeholder='blur'`/`blurDataURL`. On the slow Iraqi mobile networks called out as the priority, AVIF at q=60-65 is visually identical to q=75 but meaningfully smaller, and the absence of any LQIP/blur means every image paints blank then pops in (perceived-perf + minor CLS where aspect isn't strictly reserved).

Generate a tiny blurDataURL at build/upload time (Supabase Storage assets) and pass `placeholder='blur'` so images fade in from a blur instead of popping from blank — improves perceived LCP and removes flash on slow connections. Ensure every image sits in an aspect-ratio-locked box (product card already uses aspect-[4/3], gallery aspect-square — extend to category/brand-story).

Minor correction: hero_image.tsx and brand_story.tsx pass `unoptimized`, so quality is a no-op there (only the blur/LQIP + aspect-lock half of the fix applies); quality tuning genuinely applies to product-card/pdp_gallery/category_grid. CLS claim is marginal since product-card (aspect-[4/3]), pdp_gallery & category_grid (aspect-square) already reserve aspect. Accurate P3 perceived-perf/byte-budget enhancement, not a bug.

title: No canonical URLs and no metadataBase → duplicate-content risk across path/subdomain/custom-domain modes; relative OG images resolve incorrectly
evidence: Grep for 'metadataBase', 'alternates', 'canonical' across apps/storefront returned zero source hits (only checkout.ts comment 'canonical prices'). The same tenant is reachable via /s/scheniders-iraq (path mode), a subdomain, and a custom domain (layout.tsx:24-27 getTenantByCustomDomain + storeBase header logic at layout.tsx:38-39), but NO page sets alternates.canonical, so all three URLs are independently indexable duplicates with no canonical pointer. Without metadataBase, any relative og image (e.g. /favicons/...) Next emits is invalid for crawlers (Next warns at build).
rootCause: Multi-tenant multi-domain architecture was built without a canonical strategy; metadata generators never compute an absolute origin per tenant (custom domain vs platform subdomain vs /s/slug).

Set metadataBase to that origin in each generateMetadata, and add alternates:{ canonical: <absolute page path> } on home, PDP, category and all content pages. This also makes og:image absolute and de-dupes the three URL forms.
note: Verified: root layout.tsx:19-22 has metadata with no metadataBase; tenant layout generateMetadata (243-262), home page.tsx:19-30 (via resolveV2PageMetadata), and PDP products/[slug]/page.tsx:41-49 all emit title/desc/og but no alternates.canonical and no metadataBase. Grep across storefront source confirms zero hits for metadataBase/alternates/canonical (only a checkout.ts comment + node_modules). resolveV2PageMetadata (storefront-runtime.ts:20-44) also sets neither. Custom-domain (getTenantByCustomDomain, tenant.ts:69) + subdomain (x-store-base header, layout.tsx:39) + /s/slug all index the same tenant with no canonical pointer = real dup-content risk. No sitemap.ts/robots.ts in the app. og-image-absolute concern is secondary (stored OG URLs are usually absolute Supabase Storage), but canonical/metadataBase gap is real. P1 calibrated correctly.

title: Home & tenant metadata: no og:image fallback, no og:type/og:url, twitter card defaults to small 'summary' (no large-image preview)
evidence: apps/storefront/app/s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:256-260 builds openGraph but only spreads images when `seo?.og_image_url` exists — no fallback to the logo or a generated OG card, so a tenant without seo.og_image_url (this tenant — brand_kit.identity.og_image_url is sourced from store_config.seo at layout.tsx:125 and is empty) ships NO og:image. rootCause: OG/Twitter metadata was implemented as a thin happy-path mapping with no fallback and no twitter card; the V2 PageMeta type (packages/shared/src/types/store-config-v2.ts:77-82) has only title/description/og_image_url/noindex — no twitter or og:type field.

(2) Always set twitter:{ card:'summary_large_image', title, description, images }. (3) Set openGraph.type='website' (home) / pass through 'product' on PDP, and openGraph.url=canonical. (4) Add og:image width/height (1200x630) when known.
note: All technical claims verified true: layout.tsx:256-259 spreads og images only when seo.og_image_url exists (no logo/generated fallback); storefront-runtime.ts:36-42 resolveV2PageMetadata omits twitter/og:type/og:url; PageMeta type (store-config-v2.ts:77-82) has only title/description/og_image_url/noindex; zero twitter: metadata keys in any storefront/sections source (only lucide icons + html-embed comments), so Next defaults to twitter:card=summary; no opengraph-image/twitter-image route exists; PDP (products/[slug]/page.tsx:44-47) repeats the same pattern. title: TikTok Pixel ships placeholder id (sdkid=CABCDEF) firing live POSTs and console 'Invalid pixel ID' — pollutes analytics & adds a 3rd-party request on every page

title: Hero secondary/WhatsApp CTA renders invisible (white text + icon on white background, ~1:1 contrast)
evidence: crop-hero.png shows the empty white pill to the right of the green 'تسوّق الآن' button with no visible label or icon. Root cause: hero_image.tsx:182 renders the secondary CTA as <ChunkyButton bg="white">. In primitives.tsx the BG_VAR map (lines 149-156) has NO entry for 'white', so surfaceStyle('white') (lines 158-166) returns no foreground color. The button therefore inherits text color from its ancestor — the hero BentoCard is rendered bg="ink" (hero_image.tsx:89) and ink surfaces set color:#fff via BG_VAR.ink (primitives.tsx:155) and BG_MAP.ink 'text-white' (line 141). Proposed fix (add white:{bg:"#ffffff",fg:"var(--bk-ink,#1a1a1a)"} to BG_VAR) is correct. P0: invisible WhatsApp/contact CTA on hero breaks a primary conversion path for COD stores, confirmed live.

title: Infinite marquees (promo bar, marquee_strip, hero_marquee, logo_strip) ignore OS prefers-reduced-motion
location: apps/storefront/app/globals.css:183-232 (only reduced-motion rule at 224); tailwind.config.ts:117-125; app/s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:169,233; packages/sections/src/{helpers/primitives.tsx:99,marquee_strip.tsx:98,hero_marquee.tsx:68,logo_strip.tsx:102}
evidence: globals.css has exactly two motion media queries (grep on lines 224 & 180-190): the scroll-reveal correctly gates on `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` (line 224), but the `animate-marquee` utility (tailwind.config.ts:117-122, 'marquee 22s linear infinite') is only suppressed by the tenant-level `[data-bk-motion="reduce"]` selector (globals.css:183-190) — there is NO `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule that stops it. animate-marquee is used in PromoBar (primitives.tsx:99), marquee_strip.tsx:98, hero_marquee.tsx:68, logo_strip.tsx:102. A user with OS reduced-motion ON (and a tenant whose brand-kit motion is enabled, the default) sees these scrolling infinitely — a WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause/Stop/Hide) + 2.3 motion violation.
rootCause: Reduced-motion handling was wired only to the per-tenant brand-kit toggle ([data-bk-motion="reduce"]), not to the OS-level user preference, so marquee animations escape it for users relying on the system setting.
fix: Add a global OS-preference reset in globals.css: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .animate-marquee, [class*="animate-"] { animation: none !important; } }` (and stop the scroll-reveal, already gated). Keep the existing [data-bk-motion="reduce"] override. This honors both the OS setting and the tenant toggle.
note: Real and accurately located. Verified: globals.css has only ONE prefers-reduced-motion rule (line 224, gating scroll-reveal on no-preference); no (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) reset exists. animate-marquee = 'marquee 22s linear infinite' (tailwind.config.ts:118) is suppressed only by [data-bk-motion="reduce"]. Confirmed default is auto: app/s/[tenant]/layout.tsx:169 sets bkMotion="reduce" only when motion.enabled===false, else "auto" — so an OS-reduced-motion user on a default tenant gets infinite marquees. All 4 usage sites confirmed (primitives.tsx:99, marquee_strip.tsx:98, hero_marquee.tsx:68, logo_strip.tsx:102). Genuine WCAG 2.2.2/2.3.3 concern. Adjusted severity P1->P2: non-blocking, motion-only, affects only OS-reduced-motion users on motion-enabled tenants; content stays readable. Proposed @media reduce reset is correct.

title: No <main> landmark on the storefront page body (only <header>/<footer>)

title: text-bk-ink-faint (25% opacity ink ≈ #bfbfbf) used for real text fails contrast badly
evidence: brand-kit-vars.ts:282 defines `--bk-ink-faint = rgba(ink, 0.25)`. tailwind.config.ts:82 maps text-bk-ink-faint to it. It is used as meaningful TEXT in: product-card.tsx:130 the strikethrough compare-at price (`text-bk-ink-faint line-through` — the original price a shopper needs to read to judge the discount), product-card.tsx:108 the 'No image' fallback label, checkout_form.tsx:254 the '(اختياري)' optional hint, checkout_form.tsx:179-185 area placeholder context. For the strikethrough old price and other readable hints, switch to --bk-ink-soft (0.6) at minimum, and bump ink-soft itself to ~0.65-0.7 alpha so it clears 4.5:1 on white and on cream. Specifically change product-card.tsx:130 to text-bk-ink-soft and checkout_form.tsx:254 '(اختياري)' to text-bk-ink-soft.
note: All 4 locations verified verbatim. brand-kit-vars.ts:282 `inkFaint = rgba(ink, 0.25)`; tailwind maps text-bk-ink-faint to it. Used as real text: product-card.tsx:130 strikethrough compare-at price, :108 "No image" label, checkout_form.tsx:254 "(اختياري)" hint. title: Hero secondary CTA is white-on-white (invisible) — ChunkyButton bg="white" has no foreground color and inherits the dark card's text-white

In primitives.tsx, BG_MAP.white = "bg-white" (line 134) with NO text color, and BG_VAR has no "white" entry (lines 149-156), so surfaceStyle() returns no `color` for white (lines 158-166). The button therefore inherits text color from its ancestor: the hero BentoCard is `bg={hasImage ? "ink" : "butter"}` (hero_image.tsx:89) and BG_MAP.ink = "bg-candy-ink text-white" (primitives.tsx:141). With an image present the whole card is text-white, so the white button's label + the currentColor WhatsApp glyph (primitives.tsx:382 fill="currentColor") render white → 1:1 contrast.

Verify no white-on-dark regressions where white was intentionally on a light card.
note: Trace holds exactly. hero_image.tsx:182 renders ChunkyButton bg="white" inside BentoCard bg="ink" (hasImage true, line 89). BG_MAP.ink="bg-candy-ink text-white" (primitives.tsx:141) puts text-white on the card; BG_MAP.white="bg-white" (line 134) sets no fg and BG_VAR has no "white" key (149-156), so surfaceStyle returns no color (158-166) and buttonStyle inherits white. The cta_group div (hero_image.tsx:152-156) sets no color reset, so text-white cascades to the button. WhatsAppIcon uses fill="currentColor" (primitives.tsx:382) → white glyph + white label on white pill. Screenshot crop-hero.png shows the empty white pill right of the green CTA — invisible. Secondary CTA is the WhatsApp/call contact path (key COD conversion action), broken whenever hero has an image (default case). Proposed fix (add white:{bg:"#ffffff",fg:"var(--bk-ink,#1a1a1a)"} to BG_VAR) is the correct single-point root-cause fix matching the existing variant pattern.

title: No per-section error boundary — a single section that throws during render takes down the entire storefront page
location: packages/sections/src/RenderSection.tsx:108-150 (Render unguarded at 147; reason union line 82); packages/sections/src/_lazy-section.tsx:26-43; apps/storefront/app/error.tsx:1-30
evidence: RenderSection.tsx guards only against unknown type + schema-invalid (returns null), but the actual `<Render>` call (line 147) is unguarded — any runtime throw inside a section (bad data shape the Zod schema didn't catch, e.g. a non-array where code does `.map`, or a thrown Image error) propagates up. There is exactly one error boundary in the app: apps/storefront/app/error.tsx (route-level). There is no React error boundary around individual sections (grep for ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch in apps/storefront+packages/sections returns nothing). So one broken section = whole page blank instead of degrading that one section.
rootCause: Resilience was built for config-time failures (unknown type, schema) but not render-time throws; sections render directly with no isolating boundary.
fix: Wrap each `<Render>` in a small client ErrorBoundary in RenderSection that, on catch, calls reportSectionDrop("render_error", type, err) and renders null (in prod) / a dev placeholder. This contains a faulty section to its own slot, matching the existing silent-degrade contract for unknown/invalid types.
note: Confirmed real: RenderSection.tsx:147 calls <Render> with no React error boundary; guards at 114-124 only cover unknown_type/schema_invalid (reportSectionDrop union line 82 has no render_error). LazySection is a plain div (no componentDidCatch). Source-only grep for ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError across apps/storefront+packages/sections returns nothing (prior 6MB hit was .next artifacts). Only boundary is route-level app/error.tsx, which blanks the whole page. Severity adjusted P1->P2: mitigated by Zod safeParse on every section's props (narrows render-time-throw surface to image/runtime errors on schema-valid data) plus an existing graceful route error page — meaningful resilience gap, not a likely/constant failure.

title: LazySection reserves a flat 1200px content-intrinsic-size per below-fold section, inflating scroll height and creating phantom blank space below the fold
location: packages/sections/src/_lazy-section.tsx:26-43 (default never overridden) + RenderSection.tsx:178-186 (no intrinsicSize prop) + tmp/audit/desktop-home-true.png (visible void)
evidence: RenderPage wraps every section after the first EAGER_SECTION_COUNT (=2) in <LazySection> (RenderSection.tsx:178-186). _lazy-section.tsx:28 defaults `intrinsicSize = "auto 1200px"` and applies `contentVisibility:"auto"; containIntrinsicSize: intrinsicSize` (lines 35-38) with NO per-section override ever passed. With ~7+ below-fold sections each reserving 1200px regardless of true height, the document over-reserves vertical space — matching the orchestrator's observed scrollHeight inflating to ~7543px vs ~4379px real content (≈3160px phantom void + inflated scrollbar). The `auto` keyword should let the browser use the rendered size once painted, but the fixed 1200px reservation dominates for sections that are off-screen at load.
rootCause: Every deferred section uses the same generous 1200px placeholder height with no real measurement or per-type estimate, so total reserved height far exceeds actual content.
fix: Lower the default to a conservative value (e.g. "auto 600px") AND/OR pass a per-section-type estimate from RenderSection based on instance.type (marquee/trust ≈ 120px, grids ≈ 800px, footer ≈ 500px). Better long-term: use only `content-visibility:auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto none` (size:auto) so the browser remembers the last-rendered size and stops over-reserving. Verify scrollHeight matches content after the change.
note: Real & accurately located. _lazy-section.tsx:28 defaults intrinsicSize="auto 1200px" (applied L35-38); RenderSection.tsx:182 wraps every section past EAGER_SECTION_COUNT(=2) in LazySection passing only key+sectionId — intrinsicSize is never overridden anywhere (grep confirms, no global CSS override). desktop-home-true.png shows the symptom: a large blank void below the painted category grid where unpainted below-fold sections reserved space. Caveat lowering to P2: contain-intrinsic-size:auto 1200px uses the AUTO keyword, so once a section paints the browser remembers its real size; the 1200px only over-reserves for sections never-yet-painted (off-screen at load), so the inflation is transient/self-correcting on scroll, not a permanent void a scrolling user stares at. The 7543/4379px scrollHeight numbers are asserted in prose, not in any openable file. Defect, root cause and proposed fix (per-section estimate or contain-intrinsic-size:auto none) are sound.

title: Server runtime context hardcodes breakpoint:"mobile" — any breakpoint-conditional section/variant evaluates as mobile during SSR on desktop
location: apps/storefront/lib/storefront-runtime.ts:57-59 (confirmed); consumers are packages/sections/src/RenderSection.tsx:119,161 (NOT apps/storefront/components/v2/RenderSection.tsx as cited) and apps/storefront/components/v2-page.tsx:87 (confirmed); resolver packages/shared/src/types/store-config-v2-resolver.ts:32-33,140,232; types packages/shared/src/types/store-config-v2.ts:88-92,127-135

rootCause: Breakpoint is a real input to the config resolver but is stubbed to a constant because SSR cannot know the viewport; no client hydration step refines it.

Document the constraint either way; the current silent default can hide/show wrong content on desktop.

title: Hero secondary WhatsApp pill is white-on-white (invisible) and points at a placeholder number — broken on mobile where it's the most prominent secondary CTA
